summary: The MTN Foundation Science and Technology Scholarship (STS) pays N300,000 a year until graduation to high-performing students in science and technology courses at Nigerian public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, with a separate stream for blind students (SBS) and a top-10 UTME award. Scholars also get mentorship and skills training. Winners are 300-level STEM students (or 400-level medical students) with strong CGPAs who keep their grades up.
lookfor: STS: 300-level student in a science or technology course (or 400-level medical student) at a public tertiary institution
STS: CGPA of 3.5/5.0 or 3.0/4.0 (universities and colleges of education); upper credit 3.0 for polytechnic OND-to-HND students
SBS: blind student in 200 or 300 level, any course, CGPA 2.5 (2.0 for polytechnics)
Genuine documents - MTN states all documents must be genuine and verification can take up to 90 days
Continued good grades and meeting upskilling requirements to keep the award
cycle: The 2025 round opened in April and closed 25 April 2025; the 2026 round was announced 2 May 2026 with a 31 May 2026 deadline and is now closed. Expect the 2027 round around April-May 2027; the window can be only a few weeks.

eligibility.q: Are you at a Nigerian public (government-owned) university, polytechnic, college of education or teaching hospital?
eligibility.no: STS and SBS are for public institutions only. (Only the Top 10 UTME award covers private schools, and it is automatic.)

eligibility.q: For STS: are you in 300 level of a science or technology course, or 400 level of medicine?
eligibility.no: If you are in 200 level, prepare now and apply next year. Non-STEM students can try Jim Ovia or Seplat.

eligibility.q: For STS: is your CGPA at least 3.5/5.0 (or 3.0/4.0), or upper credit 3.0 for polytechnics?
eligibility.no: Work on your grades; the cut-off is firm. Blind students should check the SBS stream (2.5 cut-off).

eligibility.q: Are you a blind student in 200 or 300 level?
eligibility.no: Not needed for STS. If yes, apply under SBS (any course, lower CGPA cut-off).

eligibility.q: Do you have a valid ID, student ID card and proof of your CGPA?
eligibility.no: Get them before the round opens (see the Documents steps).

steps.title: Pick the right stream: STS, SBS or medical
steps.why: Applying in the wrong stream gets you rejected even if you are a strong student.
do: Open the MTN Foundation scholarships page and read the table of streams.
STS: 300-level science/technology students (and 400-level medical students). SBS: blind students in 200/300 level, any course.
Write down your level, course, institution type and CGPA scale.
Note: the Top 10 UTME award needs no application; JAMB top scorers are picked automatically.
tips: In 2026 MTN gave 400 STS awards including 100 for medical students, and 100 SBS awards.
avoid: Applying from a private university for STS.
check: I know my stream and I meet its level and CGPA rule.

links.t: MTN Foundation scholarships page (rules for all streams)

steps.title: Know the real MTN channels
steps.why: MTN's name is often used in scams. The real application has been on mtn.ng and apps.mtn.ng only.
do: Bookmark www.mtn.ng/scholarships.
Only fill forms whose address starts with mtn.ng or apps.mtn.ng.
Check that the call is also announced on MTN's official social media or in national newspapers.
If unsure, email info@mtn.ng (listed on the official page) or ask your institution's scholarship desk.
tips: The application is free. Anyone asking you to pay for a form, 'processing', a test slot or 'guaranteed selection' is a scammer.
Never use an 'agent' or cybercafe operator to apply for you with their email. Use your own email and phone so the funder's messages reach you.
MTN will never ask you to buy airtime or data bundles to 'activate' a scholarship.
avoid: Clicking 'MTN scholarship' links in WhatsApp groups without checking the address.
check: I know the official page and form address.

links.t: MTN Foundation scholarships page (rules for all streams)

steps.title: Set reminders for April-May
steps.why: In 2025 the window was about two to three weeks; in 2026 about four weeks. Late starters miss it.
do: Add a weekly reminder from 1 April 2027 to check mtn.ng/scholarships.
When it opens, write the closing date and set alarms 7 days and 2 days before.
Plan your result collection (next step) for February-March so it is ready.
tips: If you will be in 300 level in the 2026/27 session, this round is for you.
avoid: Waiting for a friend to tell you it has opened.

steps.title: Get proof of your CGPA
steps.why: STS is decided by academic performance. You need clear official proof of your CGPA.
do: Ask your department or exams and records office for a signed and stamped statement of result or result transcript up to your latest semester.
Download your result from the student portal as a second copy.
For polytechnic HND students: also keep your OND result and HND admission letter.
Scan clearly into PDF.
tips: Ask early - signatures can be slow around exam time.
avoid: Entering a CGPA higher than your official record.
check: I have an official, readable CGPA document.

links.t: MTN Foundation scholarships page (rules for all streams)

steps.title: Collect ID and admission documents
steps.why: Verification checks that you are a real student at an eligible institution.
do: Find your student ID card (request a replacement now if lost).
Have a valid ID: NIN slip/card, international passport or driver's licence.
Print your JAMB admission letter and your institution's admission/acceptance letter.
Take two recent passport photographs and keep digital copies.
SBS applicants: ask your institution's special needs or disability office for a supporting letter if you need one; check the current guidance.
tips: Name your files clearly so you upload the right one.
check: All my documents are scanned and readable.

links.t: MTN Foundation scholarships page (rules for all streams)

steps.title: Set up your contact details
steps.why: MTN contacts candidates by email and phone, and results verification can take up to 90 days.
do: Use a personal email with your real name, checked daily.
Use an active phone line registered in your name.
Make sure the name on your SIM/NIN matches your school records as closely as possible.
tips: Turn on email notifications on your phone.
check: My contacts will still work in three months.

steps.title: Read and accept the terms honestly
steps.why: The form starts with terms: documents must be genuine, MTN decides eligibility, and you allow your photos/application to be used for promotion.
do: Open the form from the official page (apps.mtn.ng/scholarships/form).
Read every term. Note the 90-day verification rule.
Accept only if you agree; then choose your stream.
tips: Take a screenshot of the terms for your records.
avoid: Skipping the terms and missing a rule that disqualifies you.

steps.title: Fill the form section by section
steps.why: Past forms had sections for personal information, UTME information, course information and family background. Accuracy matters at verification.
do: Fill personal details exactly as on your ID and school records.
Enter UTME details (registration number, score) from your JAMB slip.
Enter institution, course, level and CGPA exactly as on your result.
Complete family background honestly.
Upload documents if requested, then review everything and submit.
tips: Fill it on a laptop and save notes of your answers in case the page times out.
avoid: Picking the wrong institution or course from drop-down lists.
check: I reviewed every section before submitting.

links.t: MTN scholarship application form (closed until the next round)

steps.title: Save proof and check your inbox
steps.why: You need proof of submission if anything goes wrong.
do: Screenshot the confirmation page or save the confirmation email.
Check email and SMS (including spam) daily after the deadline.
Tell a family member the expected timeframe so they help you watch for calls.
tips: Save MTN's official contact details to spot fakes.
avoid: Answering callers who ask for payment or your PIN.

steps.title: Respond to screening and verification
steps.why: Shortlisted applicants may be asked to verify documents and in some years to take an assessment; check what your invitation says.
do: Read the invitation carefully: date, place or online link, what to bring.
Bring original documents and your ID.
If there is a test, practise basic reasoning and subject questions beforehand.
Answer any phone or email verification promptly.
tips: Arrive early and dress neatly - treat it like a job interview.
avoid: Missing verification because your phone was off.

steps.title: Accept, upskill and keep your grades
steps.why: The N300,000 continues until graduation only if you meet grade and upskilling requirements.
do: Follow the award instructions to confirm acceptance and bank details through official channels only.
Join the mentorship and skills sessions offered to scholars.
Keep your CGPA above the cut-off and send results when asked.
If not selected, check whether you can apply again next year, and try Seplat, SNEPCo or Jim Ovia.
tips: Add the award and training to your CV.
avoid: Skipping the upskilling sessions - they are part of keeping the award.
check: I know what I must do each year to keep it.

faq.a: N300,000 a year until graduation (2025 and 2026 calls), if you meet grade and upskilling requirements.
Yes, for STS if you are in a public polytechnic science/technology course with an upper credit (3.0); check the level rule in the current call.

faq.q: I am in 200 level. Can I apply for STS?
faq.a: No. STS is for 300 level (400 level for medicine). Blind students in 200 level can apply for SBS.

faq.q: Do I apply for the Top 10 UTME award?
faq.a: No. It goes automatically to the highest UTME scorers.
MTN says verification can take up to 90 days; watch your email and phone.

faq.q: How do I report a scam?
faq.a: Do not pay. Contact MTN through info@mtn.ng or 300 on the MTN network, as listed on the official page.
